info.title: Portal owner control plane (A4-2 accounts, A4-3 Governance delegation)
info.description: Owner-only account control plane. Every mutation carries the account revision it is acting on, an idempotency key, and — for the destructive ones — a step-up performed in the same session. No response ever contains a password hash, a Cloudflare subject or email, a session id, or an activation credential other than on the single response that minted it.

get.summary: The owner account roster, whole or one keyset page.

200.description: Sanitized accounts: all of them without a query, one page with one.

400.description: ROSTER_QUERY_INVALID (a limit outside 1..200, an unknown key, role or state) or ROSTER_CURSOR_INVALID (a forged or malformed cursor).

409.description: ROSTER_CURSOR_CHANGED (the cursor was issued for another owner, filter or limit) or ROSTER_CURSOR_EXPIRED. Reload the roster from its first page.

get.description: With no query the whole roster is returned as before (the transition for the V1 Users screen: no `page`, no `counts`). Sending any of `limit`, `cursor`, `q`, `role` or `state` makes the read a keyset page: ordered by `username` (unique), at most `limit` accounts (default 50, maximum 200), `page` states the limit, the returned count and the next opaque cursor, and `counts` are exact and taken in the same statement as the rows. A cursor is signed, expires, and is bound to the owner it was given to and to the exact filters and limit it was issued for.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `page.next_cursor` of the previous page, unchanged. Opaque.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive contains over username and display name.

AccountSummary.description: An account as the roster may see it. §20.5 item 1 excludes hashes, tokens, Cloudflare subject/email, session ids and audit internals; this is the whole published shape.

user_id.description: Opaque and stable. Never a database sequence or an email.

role.description: The coarse product role kept for compatibility. It is NOT ownership and authorizes nothing in this plane.

account_state.description: ARCHIVED is disabled plus a retained lineage marker; no account row is ever deleted.

must_change_password.description: True means login accepts only an activation credential, so any earlier password is unreachable.

account_revision.description: Pin the next operation to this. It changes on every lifecycle write and on nothing else.

outcome.description: Refusals are recorded too. A history that shows only what worked cannot answer 'why did nothing happen when I pressed that'.

rollback_description.description: What undoing this would mean, in the imperative, for a human reading the log during an incident.

activation.description: Present ONLY on the response that minted the credential. A REPLAYED outcome never carries it: the one view has already happened, and re-revealing on every retry would make 'one view' mean 'as many as the network felt like'.

token.description: Plaintext, once, on a no-store response. Stored nowhere — not in the operation record, not in an audit row, not in a log.

code.description: STEP_UP_REQUIRED, STALE_ACCOUNT_REVISION, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_CONFLICT, ACTIVATION_ALREADY_ISSUED, OWNER_ANCHOR_PROTECTED, ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, USERNAME_TAKEN, USERNAME_INVALID.

request_id.description: Historical nested location retained for compatibility. New responses publish request_id at the top level.
Public request correlation identifier emitted by the existing error filter; not an operation or application receipt.

workspace_id.description: null means every workspace the grantee is already a member of. A grant says what somebody may do, never where they may go.

is_owner.description: The owner holds every capability through the anchor, not through a grant row — which is why a grant aimed at the owner is refused.

outcome.description: Refusals are published too: a trail of only what worked cannot answer 'why does this person still not have it'.

external_effect.description: §20.2 rule 5: delegating a Governance capability creates no Trading System command, promotes no capital and changes no source data.

RosterPage.description: has_more is true exactly when next_cursor is a string; returned_count equals the accounts returned and never exceeds limit.

RosterCounts.description: Exact, from the same statement as the page. total, by_state, by_role, locked and awaiting_first_password count the whole roster; matching counts the accounts the filters select.

AccountRoster.description: `page` and `counts` are present together, and only on a paged read.
